links.claim: An XRPL wallet needs a base reserve plus applicable owner reserves, separately from the money it intends to send. The reserve documentation lists Mainnet settings of 1 XRP per account and 0.2 XRP per owned item at access time, and warns that other networks can differ. Validators can change requirements through fee voting; these figures are a dated reference, not a permanent application constant. [1]

links.claim: Base reserve supports the account's existence; owner reserve constrains ledger objects. Escrows, offers and signer lists can affect the latter. Removing an object can release its reserve requirement. Reserves are not payments to validators, and the documentation permits reserved XRP to pay transaction costs. Treating every XRP in a balance as transferable would therefore confuse several distinct accounting concepts. [1]

Report the failed prerequisite precisely rather than silently switching assets or increasing funding authority. [1]

sources.title: How do XRPL transaction fees and fee escalation work?
sources.body:
XRPL transaction fees destroy XRP to deter spam, and the required fee can rise with load. The transaction-cost reference gives a standard minimum of 10 drops before load scaling, with separate formulas for multisigning and conditional EscrowFinish. A quoted article price, a token transfer charge and the XRP network fee are different costs; none should be inferred from another. [1]

Servers apply a local load threshold and an open-ledger threshold. A transaction can be rejected for an insufficient local fee or queued when it does not meet the current open-ledger cost. Paying a fee is not paying a validator. Conditional EscrowFinish also depends on fulfillment size, so estimating every escrow operation as a plain Payment would understate its requirements. [1]

For agent operations, I recommend querying current fee information and applying an explicit maximum before signing. Separate the maximum allowed fee from the amount offered for content. Stop if congestion requires a fee beyond that maximum. Retrying a request should retain the original business intent and reconcile an earlier submission before creating a replacement obligation; fee escalation alone does not establish whether an earlier transaction validated. [1]

An informative fee experiment should record the transaction type, offered Fee, validated result and observed network state. Compare uncomplicated Payment, escrow creation and conditional finish without declaring one observation a universal benchmark. Include an insufficient-fee case and an uncertain submission result. These are suggested tests based on the documented fee model; no throughput, future price or completion-time promise follows from them. [1]
